sections.html: The moderlieschen (Leucaspius delineatus) is the most recommended fish species for smaller garden ponds. Due to its miniature size of usually 4-5, rarely 8-12 cm it fits even the smallest ponds, which must however have a minimum depth of 80 cm in central Europe to enable survival during winter.
Moderlieschen are reliable mosquito-larvae exterminators as they love to feed on them. Anyone who has moderlieschen in the garden pond hardly ever has mosquito plagues.
Moderlieschen are completely harmless. They are schooling fish and should be kept at least in groups of 10 specimens.

As an extreme exception among the carp family, the male moderlieschen takes care of the brood. The eggs are attached in rows to reed. If you can observe a reed stalk moving although there is no wind at all, it is very likely that a male moderlieschen moves the stalk to transport oxygen-rich water to the eggs.

The name "moderlieschen" derives from an old German word meaning "small fish without mother". This small fish was often overlooked for long times. Sometimes they reproduce in large numbers and then people believed that the fish were raining from the sky. Even this legend contains some truth: the eggs of the moderlieschen are very sticky and can by chance attach to the feet of waterfowl. So the moderlieschen can colonize even formerly fish-free waterbodies via airmail.

Moderlieschen belong to the carp family.
